extracted.intended_audience: zoologists/taxonomists and naturalists studying freshwater sponges; museum curators and systematic biologists
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and exemplars for writing formal taxonomic descriptions of freshwater sponge species and higher taxa, covering morphology (sponge, skeleton, spicules, gemmules), measurements, types, distribution, biology, and comparisons with allied taxa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponge (macroscopic description)
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise account of the sponge's gross form and appearance, e.g. “_Sponge_ flat, lichenoid, never of great thickness, devoid of branches, dense in texture but very friable; colour brown, green, or whitish; oscula numerous, small, flat, distinctly star-shaped.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include growth form (flat, cushion-like, dome-shaped, spherical, spindle-shaped), thickness, branching, surface characters (hispid, smooth, nodulose), texture (friable, hard, compact), colour (fresh and in spirit), oscula and pore appearance (size, shape, star-shaped, inconspicuous), and any attachment habit (on stones, stems, floating objects). Use parallel phrasing across species for comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skeleton (structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of the skeletal architecture, e.g. “_Skeleton_ with well defined radiating and transverse fibres, which are never strong but form a fairly dense network with a small amount of spongin.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record arrangement and relative development of radiating vs transverse fibres, regularity/irregularity of reticulation, density/compactness, presence/amount of spongin, amorphous vs reticulate conditions, and how the skeleton changes from base to surface (close network at base, more diffuse externally). Mention any special skeletal features (bush-like, feathery, reticulation under external membrane).

rubrics_metrics.name: Spicules (types and characters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed morphological account of all spicule categories: skeleton-spicules, flesh-spicules (if present), gemmule-spicules, e.g. “_Spicules._ Skeleton-spicules smooth, sharply pointed, moderately stout, as a rule nearly straight. No flesh-spicules. Gemmule-spicules cylindrical, blunt or abruptly pointed, nearly straight, covered with relatively stout, straight, irregular spines...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify shape (straight, curved, sausage-shaped, amphistrongylous, amphioxous), surface ornament (smooth, roughened, minutely spined, with conical projections), tips (sharp, blunt, truncated, projections at each end), relative stoutness, presence/absence of flesh-spicules, and any distinctive features (rotulate disks, comb-like rows of spines). Distinguish clearly between free microscleres and gemmule-associated microscleres.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gemmules (structure, arrangement, and foraminal tubules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Account of gemmule morphology and arrangement, e.g. “_Gemmules_ bound together in free groups of varying numbers and forming a flat layer at the base of the sponge; each gemmule small in size, surrounded by a thick cellular coat of several layers; with a relatively long and stout foraminal tubule, which projects outwards...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record whether gemmules are free or adherent, grouped or solitary, presence/number of foraminal tubules, tubule shape (long, bent, short, thickened at tip), coats (inner/outer chitinous membranes, pneumatic layer, cellular/granular coats), arrangement and orientation of gemmule-spicules (horizontal, vertical, mosaic-like, concentric series), and whether outer membranes form fixation skirts. Note any peculiarities (two chitinous membranes separated by space, presence of spicules in inner/outer layers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurements (spicule and gemmule dimensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitative measurements of spicule dimensions and gemmule sizes, e.g. “Average length of skeleton-spicules 0.2046 mm. breadth 0.0172 mm; length of flesh-spicules 0.053 mm; length of gemmule-spicules 0.044 mm; breadth 0.0079 mm.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide average and range values for lengths and greatest diameters of skeleton-, flesh-, and gemmule-spicules and for diameters of gemmules. Give magnification levels for figures. Numerical data should accompany descriptive terms to allow comparison between taxa.

rubrics_metrics.name: TYPE specimen and repository
rubrics_metrics.description: Citation of the type material and its deposition, e.g. “TYPE.--Potts refers to the type as being in the Academy of Natural Sciences at Philadelphia.” or “TYPE in the Indian Museum.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the author’s type designation and the museum or collection holding the type(s), note co-types and distribution of type material when applicable (co-types sent to other institutions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographical distribution and localities
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary of the species' recorded range and specific localities, e.g. “GEOGRAPHICAL DISTRIBUTION.--All over Europe and N. America; also in Siberia, Australia, and S. America.” or explicit localities within India and other regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List broad distribution followed by specific localities and regions; indicate if species is included for coverage of local races; note distribution limits (only known from Bengal, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Biology, habitat, and seasonality
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural history observations concerning habitat, substrate, seasonal occurrence, associations, and behaviour, e.g. “BIOLOGY.--S. crassissima is usually found near the surface in shallow water... S. carteri flourishes best and reaches its largest size in ponds used for domestic purposes..., thrives in water thick with soap-suds.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe substrate preference (stones, bricks, stems of bulrushes, roots, floating plants), light/shade effects on colour, seasonal timing of growth and gemmule formation (rains, cold weather, summer), associations with other organisms (incolæ like Plumatella, Chironomid larvæ), and any unusual observations (cessation of flagellar currents in aquarium heat).

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic comparison and distinguishing characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit comparative diagnosis indicating how the taxon differs from nearest allies, e.g. “The species as a species is easily distinguished from all others, its nearest ally being the N. American S. ingloriformis with sparsely spined skeleton-spicules... ” or “This species is closely allied to S. fragilis, from which it may be distinguished by the curious twinned arrangement of its gemmules.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear differential characters (shape and ornament of spicules, gemmule arrangement, size and conspicuousness of oscula, presence/absence of flesh-spicules) contrasted with named related taxa to justify species delimitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Varieties and subspecies (delineation criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria used to recognise infraspecific taxa, illustrated by descriptions such as “This local race... is distinguished from the typical form mainly by the shape of its skeleton-spicules, most of which are abruptly pointed or almost rounded at the tips...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate varieties/subspecies by consistent morphological differences (spicule tip shape, gemmule-spicule form, foraminal tubule length/shape, presence/absence of spicule types) and geographic or ecological segregation. Note types and museum depositories for varieties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genus-level diagnostic features
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters defining genera and subgenera, e.g. “The structure of the sponge resembling that of Euspongilla or Ephydatia; but the gemmule-spicules bear at either end... a double vertical row of spines...” or “This genus is distinguished from Ephydatia by the nature of the free microscleres...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the diagnostic combination of characters that separate genera/subgenera (gemmule-spicule morphology: rotulate disks, comb-like spines; nature of free microscleres; skeleton architecture such as radiating vs bifurcating fibres; presence/absence of pneumatic layer). Note geographic tendencies of genera when pertinent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrations and figure citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference to plates, figures and magnifications supporting morphological descriptions, e.g. “[Illustration: Fig. 15.--Spongilla fragilis subsp. calcuttana. A=group of gemmules, × 70; B=spicules, × 240. From type specimen.]”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include figure/plate numbers, labeled parts (A, B), and magnifications. Use illustrations to document diagnostic characters (spicules, gemmules, overall habit). Cross-reference figures in the text where measurements or unusual structures are discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomenclature, synonymy, and literature citations
rubrics_metrics.description: List prior names, synonymy, and bibliographic citations for the taxon, e.g. long lists such as “Spongilla fragilis, Leidy. Spongilla lordii, Bowerbank... Spongilla contecta, Noll...” with journal citations and dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an historical synonymy with full citations (authors, journals, pages, plates, years). Use synonymy to clarify past confusion and to justify current taxonomic decisions (inclusion of local races, doubtful status of short descriptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection and field notes (types of observation and provenance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Field- and collection-level remarks such as collector, date, circumstances of finding and preservation, e.g. “My specimens, which were taken in November, were growing on the roots of trees at the edge of an artificial pool...” and “In Prof. Weber's specimens I have found numerous small tubules of inorganic debris...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record collector names, dates, exact situation (tank, lake, conduit), depth/position (near surface, attached to lower surfaces), condition when collected (dry with gemmules, submerged), and any handling notes (dry vs in spirit, aquarium behaviour). These data inform biology, seasonality, and potential preservation artifacts.
